dispositions.reason: Filling corporate blanks and extending the LargeCo defined party to include its Affiliates is administrative and does not shift risk.
Standard carve-out excluding passive-investor portfolio companies from 'Affiliates'; does not affect LargeCo, a publicly traded company.
Removing PCI DSS from Applicable Law and narrowing to court orders relating to the parties' performance matches the deal's actual scope, which does not involve payment card data.
Correct that a private settlement agreement is not itself 'law'; the narrowing is technically sound and low-risk.
No PCI data is in scope for this pilot.
No custom Deliverables or Derivative Works are created under this SaaS-access pilot; AI Outputs are separately protected under Section 2.3.
Consistent with the deal's SaaS-access structure; outputs remain protected elsewhere.
Minor conforming edit consequential to the Deliverables cleanup.
No bespoke development occurs under this pilot, so the narrower Provider Technology definition has no practical effect on LargeCo.
The new Usage Data definition is limited to interaction/telemetry metadata and expressly excludes LargeCo Data, so it does not touch candidate content or undermine the no-training commitment.
AgentCo followed through on its own suggestion with an appropriately scoped definition.
Usage Data use is limited to service operation/improvement and third-party sharing is barred unless aggregated and anonymized; candidate data is excluded by definition.
Deleting the no-precedent clause would let pilot-scoped, cost-driven concessions bind a future full-scale engagement; we're restoring it.
We want future business with AgentCo too, but a successful pilot should be negotiated on its own terms, not inherit pilot-only concessions.
Restoring worldwide scope matches LargeCo's global footprint; the new compliance condition needs a comment flag given there is no Term/Termination section defining cure rights.
AI Outputs need IP as well as confidentiality protection, and the Agreement needs an explicit scope/no-autonomous-decision limitation that does not currently exist anywhere in the document.
A same-vendor representation today doesn't protect LargeCo if the AI stack changes during the pilot; we need a conditional flow-down obligation to survive.
We're glad it's homegrown today, but the contract needs to address what happens if that changes.
We can live without an unqualified accuracy warranty, but LargeCo's AI-governance review needs Provider's continued cooperation on how the AI Technology operates.
Conforming cross-reference updates to the renamed Exhibit C and removal of an IP-assignment flow-down that only mattered for Deliverables/Derivative Works, which don't exist in this deal.

The new restriction on submitting specially-protected data is reasonable in principle but is broad enough to sweep in ordinary EEO self-identification fields that appear in standard job applications within the approved workflows.
Reasonable for AgentCo to review LargeCo policies before agreeing to abide by them; we'll share the applicable policies.
We'll provide the relevant policies for review ahead of signature.
The Provider Technology sublicense for Deliverables is redundant with the Access Grant since no Deliverables exist; LargeCo's rights in the Service are unaffected.
Correct characterization of a SaaS-access model with no separate Deliverables IP grant needed.
The restructured Feedback clause is at least as protective of LargeCo as the original.
LargeCo's core data-ownership language survives; we're only restoring 'minimum' to keep the data-minimization principle explicit.
The deleted assignment-back language addressed Derivative Works of Data, which don't arise here; AI Outputs ownership is independently secured in Section 2.3.
No Deliverables exist under this engagement; implementation work is service configuration, not custom deliverables.
Consistent with the SaaS-access, no-Deliverables structure of the deal.
Conditioning export-support effort on a signed Order Form (not the underlying export right itself) and removing the PCI DSS disposal reference are proportionate to scope.

Removing the injunctive-relief remedy leaves LargeCo with damages-only recourse for a confidentiality or data-security breach, which is inadequate given the sensitivity of candidate data; we're restoring it.
AgentCo's own comment proposed a dispute carve-out as an alternative to outright removal; we're implementing that alternative.
Adopting AgentCo's own suggested fix rather than losing the protection outright.

Softened representations and warranties (industry-standard vs. highest-standard language, removal of a no-past-complaints warranty, removal of a physical-defect warranty irrelevant to software) are proportionate for a smaller, lower-cost vendor and don't touch data security, confidentiality, or no-training commitments.
A standard 12-months'-fees cap for ordinary claims with a 5x-fees carve-out for data-protection and confidentiality breaches matches the stronger-remedy requirement for those categories.
Flagging an apparent leftover reference to an undefined party name from another template; this needs correcting for the clause to read consistently.

Narrowing indemnification to IP infringement alone drops coverage for exactly the risk categories (confidentiality, data protection, willful misconduct) that need stronger remedies, and drops LargeCo Affiliates as indemnified parties; we're restoring both.
IP-only indemnification leaves LargeCo unprotected for the breach categories the playbook flags as needing the strongest remedies.
A 99.5% uptime commitment and shorter maintenance-notice windows are realistic for a Series A vendor at this deal size.
Accepting the response/resolution-time split as proposed, but restoring an escalation plan scoped to Critical Severity issues per AgentCo's own suggested alternative.
Committing to Response Times without Resolution Times is a reasonable middle ground for this vendor.
Same escalation-plan fix as p-112; implementing AgentCo's own Critical-severity alternative rather than losing escalation planning entirely.
Adopting AgentCo's own proposed alternative (Critical Severity only) instead of full removal.
Automatic Uptime-based Service Credits remain intact; removing automatic credits tied specifically to response/resolution/recovery misses is a reasonable SLA-realism trade for this vendor.
Core availability-based credits remain automatic; that's the remedy that matters most.
Standard, reasonable SLA exceptions (internet outages, LargeCo-caused issues, post-Term use) that any vendor would need.
These exceptions reflect LargeCo's own obligations and don't shift unrelated risk.
Conforming, low-risk wording changes to the Updates provision.

We can accept a relaxed Recovery Point Objective and a lighter disclosure of raw DR test results, but an open-ended RPO with no outer bound is not an acceptable data-loss exposure for candidate records.
We're not asking for raw test results back, only a defined outer bound on data loss exposure.
AgentCo's own comment proposed a repeated-failure threshold as an alternative to full removal; we're implementing that alternative rather than losing the termination remedy entirely.
Adopting AgentCo's own proposed compromise (termination after a pattern of failures, not a single miss).
Reduced CGL/Workers' Comp limits are proportionate to a limited six-month pilot with a smaller vendor.

Reduced Professional Liability limits and tail period, and removal of the media-specific extension, are proportionate to deal size; the underlying risk (IP infringement, confidentiality breach) is independently addressed through indemnification.
Proportionate for this vendor and deal size; substantive protection is carried by the indemnification and confidentiality provisions instead.
Pollution Liability coverage is irrelevant to a software vendor with no physical operations touching LargeCo.
Not applicable to a SaaS vendor's risk profile.
Reduced Crime insurance limit is proportionate to deal size.

Removing Additional Insured status entirely (rather than narrowing it, as AgentCo did elsewhere) would leave LargeCo without direct access to Provider's insurance proceeds for a covered claim; we're restoring a scoped version.
Scoping the Waiver of Subrogation and Primary/Non-Contributory endorsements to Provider's own negligence or indemnity obligations is a reasonable, standard limitation.
This deletion is part of the same Additional Insured rollback; restoring alongside p-170.
Limiting Provider's obligation to the stated minimum limits is standard and proportionate.

The wholesale swap from LargeCo's prescriptive security exhibit to AgentCo's generic controller-processor DPA is acceptable for the bespoke controls the playbook already says to concede (source-code review, monthly scans, equipment approval, facility access, background-check hand-over, PCI DSS), but drops core commitments the playbook requires (encryption, SSO/role-based access, audit logging, incident response, a bounded breach-notice window); raising these via comment since the region has no anchorable surviving text.

We can rely on SOC 2 in lieu of a bespoke audit right, but it needs to be a standing annual delivery obligation and needs to be paired with explicit encryption/access-control/audit-log/incident-response/breach-notice commitments that the current DPA doesn't state.
General pointer comment with no independent substance beyond the tracked edits already addressed elsewhere.
Usage Data collection for AgentCo's internal business use is already addressed by the negotiated Section 2.3 language; confirming no elevated site access is implied.
No PCI data is in scope for this pilot.
The playbook already treats background-check evidence hand-over as a control to reserve for future, more privileged integrations; a hire-time warranty is sufficient for this pilot.

Acknowledging the missing Term/Termination, Governing Law, Assignment, Force Majeure, Waiver, Severability, and Use of Name sections; LargeCo will follow up with its positions rather than guessing at terms not in the playbook.
